title: Fixing a racy counter
statement: Two std::threads each run `for (int i = 0; i < 1000000; i++) counter++;` on a shared global `int counter = 0;`. The main thread joins both and then prints counter. Which changes guarantee that it prints 2000000? Pick every one that applies.
choices: Declare counter as std::atomic<int> and keep counter++
Keep int counter but lock a shared std::mutex with std::lock_guard around counter++
Declare counter as std::atomic<int> and use counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed)
